predicate: (phase==0) & (t>=3) & (t<=6) & isin(prev_tok,[tok(c) for c in "tvdic"]) & isin(prev2_tok,[tok(c) for c in "wctsuvd"]) & isin(first_tok,[tok(c) for c in "grlnsc"])
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.02% of steps), fires only in the original (input) phase, at steps 3-8 (peaking at t=4-5), and never on the delimiter or during copying. Activating sequences tend to begin with a prefix built from a small set of consonants: first token g/r/l (also n/s/c), then s/n/c/w, then w/c/t/u, then t/v/d. The feature fires on the token right after that prefix, most often k/d/z/f/y/3, and sometimes on the next one or two tokens too. The strongest examples are prefixes like g s w v, r n c t, r c t v. It reads like a particular hidden-state direction reached by such prefixes, not like a single token. No boolean predicate captured it: the best (step 3-6, previous token t/v/d/i/c, token two back w/c/t/s/u/v/d, first token g/r/l/n/s/c) gets about 49% of activation mass at only ~6% precision on dev. Tighter conditions on token position raised precision to ~29% but cut recall to ~10%. Magnitude seemed highest for the full g/r + w/c + t/v prefix pattern, but this was not checked quantitatively.
